figurative_meaning_bn: ঔদ্ধত্য স্পর্ধা দেখানো; গ্রাহ্য না করা; সহ্যের সীমা অতিক্রম করা
figurative_meaning_en: Showing arrogance and haughtiness; disregarding advice; exceeding the limits of tolerance
similar_in_english: Getting too big for one's boots
Biting off more than one can chew
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে বাড়া বাড়া করে সবাইকে অস্বস্তিতে ফেলে দিচ্ছে।
বাড়া বাড়া করলে শেষে লজ্জায় পড়তে হবে।
example_sentences_in_english: He is acting too arrogant and making everyone uncomfortable.
If you keep getting too big for your boots, you'll end up humiliated.
history: This idiom metaphorically refers to a plant or tree that grows excessively tall and becomes vulnerable to being uprooted by strong winds, symbolizing the dangers of unchecked pride in Bengali oral traditions.
note: Often used in rural and semi-urban Bengali contexts to advise against hubris.
